ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, circle $\odot O$ is inscribed in square $ABCD$ with $O$ as its center. Let $\angle MON=90^\circ$ with its two sides intersecting $BC$ and $CD$ at points $M$ and $N$ respectively, and intersecting $\odot O$ at points $E$ and $F$. If $CM+CN=6$, what is the length of arc $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let circle $O$ be tangent to side $CD$ of square $ABCD$ at point $G$ and to $BC$ at point $H$, as shown in the solution diagram. Connect $OG$ and $OH$. Then, quadrilateral $OHCG$ is a square. \\
Since $\angle GON+\angle NOH=90^\circ$ \\
and $\angle HOM+\angle NOH=90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle GON=\angle HOM$, \\
Also, since $\angle OGN=\angle OHM=90^\circ$, \\
and $OG=OH$, \\
thus $\triangle OGN \cong \triangle OHM$ (ASA), \\
therefore $GN=HM$ \\
Hence, the radius of circle $O$ is $= \frac{1}{2}(CM+CN)=3$ \\
Therefore, $\overset{\frown}{EF}=\frac{90}{180}\times 3\pi =\boxed{1.5\pi}$.

With OG = OH = r and right angles at G and H, triangles OGN and OHM are congruent, giving GN = HM. Then express CM = CH + HM and CN = CG − GN; because CH = CG = r and HM = GN, get CM + CN = 2r. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, circle $\odot O$ is inscribed in square $ABCD$ with $O$ as its center. Let $\angle MON=90^\circ$ with its two sides intersecting $BC$ and $CD$ at points $M$ and $N$ respectively, and intersecting $\odot O$ at points $E$ and $F$. If $CM+CN=6$, what is the length of arc $EF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let circle $O$ be tangent to side $CD$ of square $ABCD$ at point $G$ and to $BC$ at point $H$, as shown in the solution diagram. Connect $OG$ and $OH$. Then, quadrilateral $OHCG$ is a square.
Since $\angle GON+\angle NOH=90^\circ$ and $\angle HOM+\angle NOH=90^\circ$, thus $\angle GON=\angle HOM$.
Also, since $\angle OGN=\angle OHM=90^\circ$ and $OG=OH$, thus $\triangle OGN \cong \triangle OHM$ (ASA), therefore $GN=HM$.
Hence, the radius of circle $O$ is $\frac{1}{2}(CM+CN)=3$.
Therefore, $\overset{\frown}{EF}=\frac{90}{180}\times 3\pi=\boxed{1.5\pi}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure, the vertex positions of square ABCD are A at the upper left, B at the upper right, C at the lower right, and D at the lower left; circle O is inscribed in the square, and O is the center of the circle. Two rays starting from O form a right angle, one of which goes up to the right, passes through E on the circle, and then intersects the right side BC at M, and the other goes down to the right, passes through F on the circle, and then intersects the lower side CD at N.

Reasoning: Let the tangency point of the circle with the right side BC be H, and the tangency point with the lower side CD be G, and connect OH and OG. Because the circle is inscribed in the square, OH ⟂ BC, OG ⟂ CD, and OH = OG = r. Also because H, C, and G are respectively on the right side and the lower side, quadrilateral OHCG is a square with side length r, therefore CH = CG = r.

From the positions in the figure, it can be known that ON is between OG and OH, and OM is above OH. Because ∠GOH = 90°, ∠GON + ∠NOH = 90°; also it is known that ∠MON = 90°, and ∠MON = ∠HOM + ∠NOH, so ∠GON = ∠HOM.

In right triangles OGN and OHM, ∠OGN = ∠OHM = 90°, OG = OH = r, and ∠GON = ∠HOM, therefore △OGN ≅ △OHM, so GN = HM.

Thus CM = CH + HM = r + HM, CN = CG - GN = r - GN. Adding gives CM + CN = 2r + HM - GN = 2r. It is known that CM + CN = 6, so 2r = 6, r = 3.

E and F are at the intersection points of the two mutually perpendicular rays OM and ON with the circle, so the corresponding central angle ∠EOF = ∠MON = 90°. The length of arc EF is (90/360)·2πr = (1/4)·2π·3 = 3π/2.
